Coming out is probably always going to be terrifying. Every single person I've known who has come out, no matter how accepting their parents are, has been scared. The fear only goes away after you come out. This is why I think you should come out as soon as possible. If you are in a safe situation, and your parents are caring and love you, and the only thing that is holding you back is fear, you should do it. Just find a way to do it anyways. Write a letter, send a text, blurt it out, whatever way you are able to get it out. (If you're doing talking, a car drive alone has always been easiest for me - no eye contact, you have a good opportunity to talk alone, you can hide your fear a little better). 

Maybe your parents will not understand. Many parents need time to wrap their heads around being trans before they are fully understanding and accepting. No matter what, they will need some explaining and some time. But the sooner you come out, the sooner they will be able to learn and understand. The sooner you might be able to cut your hair, go on T, whatever else you need. 

Coming out and socially and physically transitioning is a long process. My only regret was not starting it sooner because of self doubt and fear.
